newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Jochimsen omits EMU comments from speech.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Jochimsen omits EMU comments from speech.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen omitted some comments on European economic and monetary union when delivering a prepared speech at an event in Berlin on Monday.
Earlier, Reuters reported on the basis of a prepared text of the speech that Jochimsen said a hasty start for Europe's monetary union could be more damaging than a limited delay.
"A hasty entry into EMU would create a greater damage than a limited delay," Jochimsen said in the text of the speech prepared for delivery at the inauguration of a building.

Jochimsen, who is also the president of the state central bank of North Rhine-Westphalia, also said in the text that if the currency union were to be a success then nations would need to first do their homework.
Remaining structural weaknesses would be ruthlessly underscored by a currency union, Jochimsen added.
When delivering the speech he omitted these comments, adding however that monetary union was a good project overall, but had to be based on good fundamentals.
Germany and France were essential founder members of the union, which should group as many states as possible, he added in his remarks at the inauguration.
